tldr: LLM+P is a framework that combines large language models with classical planners to solve long-horizon planning problems correctly, significantly outperforming LLMs used alone.
contributions: Introducing LLM+P, the first framework incorporating classical planners into LLMs for natural language planning
Defining a diverse benchmark set of seven robot planning domains with 20 automatically generated tasks each
Demonstrating LLM+P enables a home robot to solve complex manipulation tasks specified in natural language
methods: LLM+P takes a natural language description of a planning problem and first converts it into PDDL format using an LLM with in-context learning (providing a simple example problem-PDDL pair as context). The generated PDDL problem file is then fed into classical planners (FAST-DOWNWARD using SEQ-OPT-FDSS-1 for guaranteed optimal plans and LAMA as a sub-optimal fallback) with a maximum search time of 200 seconds. Finally, the LLM translates the PDDL plan back into natural language. Baselines compared include LLM-AS-P (direct LLM planning without a planner) and Tree of Thoughts (TOT).
results: LLM+P achieved high success rates across domains: Blocksworld 90%, Grippers 95% (100% for sub-optimal), Storage 85%, Barman 20% (100% sub-optimal), Tyreworld 10% (90% sub-optimal), and Termes 20%. In contrast, LLM-AS-P and TOT performed poorly, with most domains showing 0-25% success. LLM-AS-P failed primarily because it lacks ability to reason about preconditions (e.g., cannot track ON/CLEAR properties in Blocksworld, fails to clean shot glasses in Barman).
limitations: The LLM does not recognize when a prompt is suitable for the LLM+P pipeline; a robot must know when to trigger it
Requires a human expert to provide the domain PDDL file (automatic generation of domain descriptions is left as future work)
Some domains with complex spatial relationships (FloorTile) remain unsolved
Several domains timed out with optimal planners, requiring sub-optimal fallback
